meta.title: Saint Jude Initial World-State Seed (1975 snapshot)
meta.status: starting snapshot built from the Saint Jude Setting Bible (October 2026); for owner review
source_authority: Saint Jude Setting Bible: Index and Parts I to VI (worlds/saintjude/bible.md is its packaged form)
meta.authority_rule: The bible outranks this seed. Campaign history may add facts but may not rewrite setting canon.
meta.calendar_rule: Gregorian; day 0 is Wednesday 1 January 1975; birth_day is authoritative arithmetic and birth_date its rendering.
meta.example_rule: Every named person is an Example (Part III 4.6, Part V 0.2) with canon_tag 'Example' and may be replaced; Fixed history in the claims names no person, only roles and events.
meta.families_rule: The four families are Sabatini, Pellegrino, Ferrante and Vannucci (Part III 0). Women are never made (Part I 12.2).
meta.open_offices_rule: Offices and institutions are seeded; the names of their holders are Open (Part I 15.1, Part II 10, Index 7) and are not seeded.
meta.no_pressures_rule: No pressures, secrets, deadlines or plot hooks are stored; motives are ordinary traits.

judgement_calls: Every named person is an Example (canon_tag) and replaceable at seed. Those marked source 'seat' are the Part III 4.6 suggested seats; 'carried' are men of the old codex cast kept as Examples; 'added' were added to give an institution structure.

Part III 4.6 makes Ettore 'Eddie Glasses' Conti, Lorenzo DeLuca (37) and Jackie Pellegrino (29) capos and Salvatore Ferrante's circle a boss, underboss, consigliere and one capo; the seed follows the table. Giuseppe Vannucci is 67 (the table says about 67) and is the boss; his son is the underboss.
Pellegrino is Matteo Pellegrino's family from the start; there is no old boss above him (the old codex's invented uncle is dropped).

Declan Gallagher is aged to 58 so the Brigades are led by an older man (Part III 5.1); Liam Gallagher becomes his nephew. Brendan O'Malley no longer has a dead brother; the 1973 victim and his brother are Open.
Walter Pettiford (63) is one banker of the headless combine, matching the deacon-banker Example of Part V 4.10.

Women are a small minority and none holds a made rank: Lucia Vannucci (wife and matriarch), Teresa Ianelli (daughter, ready-mix office), Margaret Dunleavy (pub owner), Maureen Tierney (features editor) and Valerie St. Clair (singer). Routes: family, small business, female-dominated institution (Part I 12.4).
Dennis McCaffrey is made a Captain, the commander of the 14th Precinct, rather than a Lieutenant.
The seed records Design ranges for family size in the family notes; it does not roster 180 made men. Named persons are a thin layer over a much larger unnamed population.
Business valuations in economic_state come from prices_1975.json ranges; they are assumptions, not accounts.
Nicknames are in public_identity_text as street names; no secret, pressure or plot hook is attached to any of them.

places.notes: District Seven. A windswept peninsula on the Atlantic, north-east of the Eastside and joined to it by the Shore Parkway: brick apartment blocks, boarding houses, a boardwalk and a pier with a shuttered amusement park. Elderly Jewish and Eastern European retirees; Soviet Jewish emigrants have been arriving since 1971, a few thousand by 1975. The 21st Precinct.

places.notes: District Two. The downtown at the head of the Basin, on the old Dutch trading-post site (Fort Kroon, renamed 1664). Art Deco towers, banks, law firms, department stores losing customers to suburban malls, steakhouses and the federal complex. Sabatini ground; violence here draws everyone's attention at once.

places.name: The Eastside
places.notes: District Six. East of the Hill and downtown running to the sea: the garment district, the rail yards and produce terminal, public housing and Dunmore Avenue, the heart of Black Saint Jude. The city's poorest district since the 1950s. It burned in July 1967 and again in April 1968; the I-95 Crosstown Expressway displaced about 4,000 families.

places.name: Kerrytown
places.notes: The Bricks. Irish ground; Italian men rarely enter after dark without a reason. The 11th Precinct.

Outside the SJPD's jurisdiction, policed by a borough force of about twenty officers; the Gold Coast Sanctuary is a convention that no gunfire, sirens or bodies come here.

places.name: Saint Jude
places.notes: Fictional Atlantic port city on the Killbuck River in the real State of New Jersey (Part I 3.1a). About 1.1 million people in the city, which is also Killbuck County, and about 2.4 million in the metropolitan area; about 105 square miles. Founded in the 1640s as a Catholic refuge on the south bank. Eight districts plus the smaller worlds of Part I 6.

Home to all four families, the one district where they cannot avoid each other. The Elevated (the Hill Line) runs along Via Garibaldi. Split between the 3rd and 4th Precincts.

claims.text: The present St. Jude's Cathedral was built from 1868 to 1884 in brownstone and granite on the site of the original chapel, whose foundation stones lie under the north transept. The Archdiocese of Saint Jude was erected in the nineteenth century and St. Jude's became its cathedral.
In 1974 the Sabatini boss of the day took the Concrete Club into his own hands. A brother-in-law and three contractors are gone. What happened to them is Open; the city has only rumor.

claims.text: In 1973 Pellegrino crews used cargo hooks and shotguns to crush an independent longshoremen's strike on the South Piers. A Kerrytown longshoreman was killed; his brother is still in Kerrytown. Who they were is Open. Kerrytown does not forget.

From 1970 to 1972 the Dolan Commission, a mayor's investigation into police corruption, sorted the SJPD into grass-eaters and meat-eaters. Several officers went to prison and the Commissioner resigned; plainclothes gambling squads were broken up and cops were rotated through precincts. Which officers were convicted and which reforms stuck are Open.
claims.provenance: Part I 2.5, Part II 2.6 (Fixed; details Open)

claims.text: In 1958 the Ferrante crews of the East side broke from the Sabatinis in a six-month civil war. They had too many gunmen to be put down and became the Ferrante Family, the city's fourth family. Who started it, and why, is Open.

claims.text: Saint Jude began in the 1640s as a small Roman Catholic refuge on the south bank of the Killbuck: Catholic families and one chaplain driven out of other colonies, settling where the river bends, with a Dutch trading post across the water that the English renamed Crown Harbor in 1664. The settlers dedicated their chapel to Saint Jude, the neglected apostle, patron of desperate cases.

In 1946 the Four-Corner Harbor War, a short, brutal war for the four corners of the harbor (the North Piers, the South Piers, the Basin and the Narrows), ended in exhaustion and set the divide of the Iron Balance. The names of the dead are Open.

The Prohibition years made the families here. In the Harbor wars of 1929 to 1931 among the Italian combinations, the Sabatini and Pellegrino combinations came out on top. Who really won is told differently by different people.

In July 1967, the same month the Eastside burned and when no one in the Pellegrino family was watching the Flats, the old Vannucci boss took the Mercer Avenue and Ironworks crews out of the Pellegrino family and became the Vannucci Family.
After a newspaper series and state hearings exposed the docks in 1949 to 1953, the State created the Killbuck Waterfront Commission in 1954 to register longshoremen and stop the shape-up.
